THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE          45

SOPHOMORE YEAR

        Geometry, Trigonometry, Surveying
        Virgil, Cicero
        Homer, Livy
        Xenophon’s Memorabilia, Demosthenes’ de Corona
        Physics
        Elocution

SENIOR YEAR

        Calculus, Astronomy
        Tacitus, Quintilian’s Letters
        Homer’s Iliad          Prometheus of Aeschylus,
        Phaedo of Plato, Clouds of Aristophanes

    By the year 1887-1888 this curriculum had been strengthened and re-formed in a number of significant ways:

    Elocution had been added to the Freshman year’s work; Composition and Declamation to the Sophomore and Senior; and a course in Botany to the Junior. A note had added “A Select Course in Reading” to the Senior.

    Physiology, absent from Sophomore to Freshman, had become Anatomy. Physiology and Hygiene. Meteorology and Botany had been added to the second year’s schedule; Zoology to the third; and Geology to the fourth.

    Ancient History enriched the new Sophomore work, as did also Logic; Mental Philosophy had been added to the Junior Schedule, and Mental and Moral Science to the Senior.

    Juvenal had been substituted for Quintilian and Pliny in the last year’s Latin authors, and the Alcestis had been dropped from the Greek reading list.

    French, or German, as alternate choices, had been added to the Freshman and Sophomore language requirements.
